narration: Two views of the same scene, captured at time tau and at time tau prime, enter the pipeline as the raw inputs.
Both views pass through the Patch Feature Extractor: one convolutional backbone E applied twice with shared weights, so the two timestamps are embedded in a common space.
Each backbone feeds a Deformable Transformer Encoder. Dashed skip links carry the earlier multi-scale feature maps forward, and the two encoders also share their weights.
The encoders emit two sequences of patch tokens, z s at time tau and z s at time tau prime, one coloured token per spatial patch.
A separate Patch Matching Network reads both views directly and produces the matching features used to relate patches across the two timestamps.
In Multi-Temporal Patch Matching the two token sequences are compared. The dashed links show which patch at time tau corresponds to which patch at time tau prime.
From those correspondences the model selects patches: matched positives for each timestamp, and unmatched patches that act as negatives.
The selected patches are pooled into three sets: the positives at tau, the positives at tau prime, and the negatives at tau prime.
The Object Residual Module subtracts a learned object prototype phi k from every patch embedding, giving a residual vector r for each sign q, each timestamp t and each scale s.
Those residuals drive two objectives: a multi-view loss that aligns the two timestamps, and a scale-regression loss that keeps the representation consistent across scales.
With the mask lifted, the whole pipeline is visible: shared patch encoding, cross-time patch matching, positive and negative selection, residual computation, and the two training losses.
